comment: Blamsoft publish no source. Input 1 is declared in the module but has no widget on the panel, so no click can reach it and it is left untagged. The unlabelled jack above the waveform display is input 7: process reads it as wavetable = menu choice + int(6.9v + 0.5), clamped to 0-69, and the panel draws a connector line from that jack to the display. V/Oct is input 5 and FM is input 6, which is the reverse of their left-to-right order on the panel; the polyphony channel count comes from input 5. Params 9, 10 and 11 are declared with no name and no widget. Each of the four trimmers maps its 0-1 position to -1 to +1 and multiplies the jack voltage by 0.1, so a fully open trimmer lets 10V cover the whole 0-1 range of the control it feeds; the sum is then clamped, so CV cannot push a control past its limits. Reset Harmonics is the only item the module's own right-click menu adds. Nothing has to be loaded or armed before the module sounds: the channel count is taken as max(1, channels at V/Oct), so it runs one voice with nothing patched there. The maker's PDF manual was read on this pass with pypdf; it supplied the table of modifier names and the gloss for Pinch, Gate, Juno, Mirror, Zoom, Wrap, In and Out, and it confirms that the three modifiers process the waveform in order except where one is switched to post. The long modifier names and the short ones the display prints are both the maker's own, and their order matches the manual's table.
